substitute.reason: referee-three failed after its one retry: ingest refused both attempts (verdict judge with a zero-width joiner)

findings.evidence: 'Passing "$NAME" or "$(cat file)" as an argv is safe: a double-quoted expansion is never re-parsed, so quotes, $, backticks and newlines stay inert.' This explains generic bash quoting that the model already knows.
findings.fix: Keep the project rule ('never paste JSON text into a command; load it with NAME="$(cat "$RUN_DIR/NAME.json")"'). Cut the explanation of why double-quoted expansions are safe, or move it to references/design-notes.md, and record the removal.

findings.evidence: The Process pattern is clear, but some single paragraphs pack several conditional rules each (line 207: round increment, resume exceptions, flagged-lane switch, restored-round routing; line 246: native model, fix-loop resume, ladder escalation, failure route, host-config audit, real-home guard). That blurs the phase checkpoints.
findings.fix: Split each overloaded paragraph into a short numbered checkpoint list inside its step, for example Step 3 native: 1 audit snapshot, 2 launch, 3 audit compare, 4 record LAST_DISPATCHED_KEY, 5 clear resume state. Keep every rule and move none out of the step.

findings.evidence: Environment facts that defy assumptions sit in Step 3 prose rather than in a Gotchas list: 'Codex runs under --codex-sandbox workspace-write ... not an unconditional boundary', 'claude has no exec formula in the runner', 'an older Node may crash, and that crash is a real_error of the pair, never a reason to switch pairs'.
findings.fix: Add a short '## Gotchas' section after the NEVER list that holds these environment facts: codex sandbox is not a boundary, claude runs only natively, pi and copilot exec are unverified, an old Node crash is a real_error, every Bash call is a fresh shell. Leave a one-line pointer in Step 3.

findings.evidence: The description triggers only when the request names the superpowers plan 'that way' (under subagent-driven-development). It does not cover a user who asks to run or continue a superpowers plan with subagents without naming the skill, and it does not mention the no-lane session-model path that trigger-queries.json counts as a positive.
findings.fix: Runs a superpowers implementation plan (docs/superpowers/plans/*.md) under superpowers:subagent-driven-development, resolving a live-quota-checked (runtime, model) pair for each task's implementer dispatch (native or external CLI), with quota waits, a session-model fallback when no execute lane exists, and fix-round escalation; it starts the plan's unit branch before the first task and folds, pushes (with consent) and readies it after the final review through ai-kit-commit-fold. Use when ai-kit-spec-execute detects a superpowers plan run under subagent-driven-development, or when asked to run, execute or continue a superpowers plan task by task with subagents or a per-task model choice, even if the user does not name subagent-driven-development or ai-kit. Not for superpowers:executing-plans (inline, no dispatch point), writing or reviewing a plan, configuring lanes (ai-kit-spec-config), or folding a branch on its own (ai-kit-commit-fold).

findings.evidence: Several single SKILL.md paragraphs run past 1000 characters (lines 152, 207, 209, 237, 246, 282). They restate rules that the gated references already own. Session-fallback and session-model behaviour appears at lines 152, 209 and 219 and again in references/resolution-stops.md, references/escalation.md and references/config-check.md. This pushes the always-loaded body well past the recommended ~5000 tokens.
findings.fix: Keep one sentence plus the MANDATORY read trigger at each of these points. Move the session-fallback detail (lines 209, 219) to references/resolution-stops.md#owner-stop, the gates and guard recipe detail (line 237) to references/state-management.md#gates-and-guard-inputs, and the native-audit detail (line 246) to references/dispatch-external-cli.md#host-config-audit, where it already partly lives. Record each move.

findings.evidence: 'Every native launch ... runs one audit: before it rm -f "$RUN_DIR/host-config-before.json" and python3 "$SHIM" host-config-audit --snapshot ..., after it python3 "$SHIM" host-config-audit --compare ..., then rm -f ...' This is a fragile four-command sequence across two calls, given as inline prose, while comparable sequences get exact blocks.
findings.fix: Give the native audit two exact bash blocks, labelled 'before the native launch' and 'after the native launch', each opened by the scalar loader, next to the print-guidance block.

findings.evidence: edge-flagged-lane-quota-switch scripts executor-fallback as {"switched": true, "key": "execute-backup"} with no 'exclude'. The Flagged switch block reads json.load(...)["exclude"] into SWITCH_EXCLUDE_JSON (empty on KeyError), and resolve-injection then fails on json.loads(""). An agent that follows the skill exactly records SWITCHED=0, which contradicts the expected output 'dispatches execute-backup in the same round'.
findings.fix: Add the real shape to the scripted answer: {"switched": true, "key": "execute-backup", "exclude": ["execute-primary"]}, matching cli.py's executor-fallback output, so the eval exercises the switch path it asserts.

findings.evidence: Nearly every should-trigger query names both 'superpowers' and 'subagent-driven-development' or the exact plan folder ('run this superpowers plan with subagent-driven-development and pick a runtime and model for each task'). Few are implicit, casual or context-rich (personal context, typos, a task buried in a longer chain).
findings.fix: Replace 3-4 positives with realistic implicit phrasings. Example: 'ok the plan in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-20-billing.md is approved, kick it off with fresh subagents per task and use codex where my quota allows', plus one with a typo and one where the run is step 3 of a longer request.

findings.evidence: 'GSD's Node floor: @opengsd/gsd-core 1.17.0 declares engines.node >=24.0.0' is a version-sensitive minimum version with no source URL and no date checked, and no instruction reads it live.
findings.fix: Cite the official package page or the package.json URL for @opengsd/gsd-core 1.17.0 with the date checked (for example 'npm view @opengsd/gsd-core@1.17.0 engines, checked YYYY-MM-DD'), or tell the agent to read it live with 'npm view @opengsd/gsd-core engines'.

findings.evidence: 'Codex runs under --codex-sandbox workspace-write (writes stay in the target dir plus /tmp, $TMPDIR and any writable root the owner's codex configuration adds ...)' states vendor CLI sandbox defaults with no source URL or date checked.
findings.fix: Add the official Codex sandbox documentation URL and the date checked for the workspace-write writable roots, in SKILL.md's Evidence section or references/design-notes.md, or mark the default as read live from 'codex --help' or the codex config docs.

findings.evidence: 'Run the block below only at a new round: a restored $FIX_ROUND already counts the round, so the resume path never runs it and goes straight to references/escalation.md's resolve block.' Following this branch for a resume restored at FIX_ROUND 1-3 sends the agent to the escalation resolve block, but escalation applies only at 4 or more (lines 211-219, escalation.md 'When it applies'), and rounds 1-3 reuse $INJECTION_JSON.
findings.fix: Reword to: 'a restored $FIX_ROUND already counts the round, so the resume path never runs it: at a restored round of 4 or more with no pinned injection_json it goes to references/escalation.md's resolve block; at rounds 1-3, or with a pinned injection, it dispatches through Step 3 unchanged.'

findings.evidence: 'One Bash call, before the Task paths block (no scalar file exists yet).' But config-check.md block 1 (GUIDANCE_READY=, CONFIG_CHECK= clear) and block 2 (CONFIG_CHECK=) already write that scalar file before the start step.
findings.fix: Change the parenthesis to '(the Task paths block has not run yet, so fill the placeholders from Step 0 and Step 1; the scalar file may already hold CONFIG_CHECK from the no-config check)'.
